prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric workspace where the camera wearer's left forearm and thigh in the lower-left foreground are nearest (brightest white, ~0.2–0.4 m away), while the right hand holding a paintbrush and the flat painting canvas/board resting on newspaper in front are slightly farther (~0.4–0.6 m), all within arm's reach. Above and slightly behind the canvas (~0.5–0.7 m away, ~0.1–0.2 m from the canvas), an upright tablet screen on the left faces toward the camera wearer, with a box of paint tubes to its right and jars in the upper-left corner, while the floor visible past the table edge on the far right drops off to the darkest values (~1.0–1.5 m below). The camera wearer's left hand occludes the bottom-left corner of the tablet and the left edge of the canvas, the right hand and brush occlude the right side of the canvas, and the wearer's torso and head remain out of view behind the camera. Across the 5 frames, the depth values show a slight downward camera tilt in frame 2 followed by an upward return in frames 3–5 as the right hand shifts slightly left and right across the canvas while maintaining a steady distance. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated plane of the table and upright tablet from the recessed floor on the right, though it looks unreliable where the thin paintbrush shaft blends into the canvas in frame 2 and where internal details of the paint tubes flatten into a uniform mid-grey.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates key foreground regions within arm's reach (~0.2–0.7 m from the camera wearer), labeling the upright tablet screen in the upper-left as 'tv' (~0.5–0.7 m away, facing the wearer), the flat painting board below it in the center as 'book' (~0.4–0.6 m), and a few paint tubes in the upper-right box (~0.6–0.7 m, ~0.1–0.2 m right of the tablet) as 'bottle'. It also labels the camera wearer's left and right arms/hands in the lower foreground (~0.2–0.5 m) as 'person', showing how the left hand occludes the upper-left edge of the central board and bottom-left of the tablet, while the right hand overlaps the right side of the board. No other people are present in the scene, and the wearer's body beyond the forearms and thighs is out of view at the bottom edge. Across the 5 frames, the masks shift slightly vertically with the camera's head movement as the right hand moves slightly toward the center of the board, while the segmentation of the arms fragments and merges into different instance colors from frame to frame. While the map provides sharp boundary contours for the tablet and central board that stand out against the cluttered newspaper background in RGB, it is highly unreliable in class labeling and consistency—misclassifying the tablet as 'tv', the canvas as 'book', paint tubes as 'bottle', and brush handles on the far left as 'book' or 'scissors', while missing most of the paint box, jars, and paintbrush.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-right foreground (~0.4–0.5 m away, within arm's reach over the right side of the canvas), while no other people are present in the scene and the wearer's head and torso are out of view. In frames 1 and 4, fragments of a yellow body skeleton appear in the lower foreground (~0.3–0.6 m away), including a cluster of points near the wearer's right foot on the floor in frame 1 and a quadrilateral torso/hip outline over the central canvas in frame 4. The right hand skeleton faces palm-down and slightly inward toward the left across all 5 frames, shifting slightly downward in frame 2 and slightly leftward across the canvas in frames 3–5 as the fingers curl around the unrendered paintbrush. This map reveals the precise 2D joint articulation of the curled right fingers even when they self-occlude over the dark brush and shadowed canvas in the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable because it completely fails to detect the prominent left arm and hand in the lower-left foreground (~0.2–0.4 m away) across all 5 frames and hallucinates an erratic yellow body box over the flat painting board in frame 4.
